_comment: THE RECORDED BASELINE for the native semantic differential. `./run.sh`
checks against this and FAILS on any new divergence family, any lost
coverage, any moved population, and any mutation the differential fails to
catch. Rewrite it only with `./run.sh [--fast] --accept`, and read the diff
before committing: accepting a baseline is accepting every divergence in it.
THE BASELINE IS NOT ZERO. Eight scalar-FP families diverge and are recorded
below. Baselining at zero would require either fixing them first or lying;
naming them is what makes the NEXT family visible when it arrives.
=== CLOSED 2026-08-10 — the three families this file used to record ===
Ldr/Str SIMD&FP, Ubfm/Sbfm with imms<immr, and Adcs/Sbcs are FIXED and no
longer diverge. Measured same-denominator under THIS harness, 522k
comparisons, by reconstructing the old model and rerunning:
Ldr   2862 -> 0     operand_to_formula now consults RegKind; the SIMD&FP
Str   2991 -> 0     load/store forms read/write the V file (read_fpr /
Effect::FpRegWrite) instead of the GPR of the same
number, and every other r.kind discard on the path
(extract_dst_reg, read_base_reg, extended_index_value,
ShiftedReg) now fails closed.
Ubfm  2814 -> 0     the imms<immr arm masks the source to imms+1 bits;
Sbfm  2394 -> 0     SBFM also sign-extends from bit imms.
Adcs   370 -> 0     the carry-out is computed FROM the carry-in:
Sbcs    86 -> 0     C = (result <u lhs) OR (carry_in AND result == lhs).
Value-pinned regressions for all three live in
crates/trust-machine-sem/src/aarch64/divergence_tests.rs; each failed before
its fix, with the observed output quoted in the test. The `fp-write-to-gpr`
and `swap-carry-overflow` entries in `nonvacuity` below are the first and
third of those bugs, re-injected on every run so the differential must keep
proving it can still see them.
=== OPEN — scalar FP, NEWLY VISIBLE, NOT NEWLY BROKEN ===
These eight families were ALWAYS diverging. They were invisible because this
harness did not load the V register file and `ConcreteState` had none, so
`Formula::Var("V0")` was an unknown variable and every word reading a SIMD
register was counted UNCHECKED. The oracle could not see the register file,
so it could not report a bug in it — which is also exactly how the Ldr/Str
family stayed open. The V file is now part of the starting state on both
sides and compared over all 32 registers.
That they are pre-existing is MEASURED, not asserted: the reconstructed old
model and the fixed model produce IDENTICAL counts for all eight, so the
three fixes neither caused nor touched them.
FmovImm 3561   Fcvtzs 1305   Scvtf 1298   Fcvtzu 1275   Ucvtf 1235
Fsqrt    464   Fcvt    447   Fcmp    141                    total 9726
Every one is a BITVECTOR APPROXIMATION of an IEEE-754 operation, several
self-declared in aarch64/fp.rs (`sem_fcvt`: "Width conversion: truncate or
zero-extend"; `sem_fcmp`: "modeled as a bitvector signed comparison
(approximation)"; the int<->FP converts likewise reinterpret bits). Confirmed
shape: `scvtf s14,w0` (9e22000e) model v14=0x200f8 — the integer's bit
pattern — native v14=0x50800040, the float. FADD/FSUB/FMUL/FDIV do NOT appear
because they are modeled bit-exactly (FpToIeeeBv(FpAdd(RNE,..))) and the
concrete replayer refuses those formula variants outright.
THE CORRECT RESOLUTION IS REFUSAL, NOT THIS BASELINE ENTRY. Per the standing
rule, approximating onto a neighbouring value is never acceptable; refusing
always is. These are recorded here so that a NINTH family is still visible
while that work is scheduled, not because approximation is being accepted.
Reachability in the emitted corpus was measured at 0 (no emitted word carries
a SIMD operand), so no shipped verdict rests on them today — but the gate
would believe them if one did.
=== HOW TO RE-DERIVE EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE ===
./run.sh --fast     ~8 s   replays population-fast.txt (committed)
./run.sh            ~25 s  rescans 2^32 and re-stratifies at cap 3000
The population does not depend on --workers (verified identical at 3, 8 and
11). Mismatch counts, opcode counts and the family set are exactly
reproducible.
ONE NUMBER IS NOT: `compared` jitters against `platform_register_x18`. That
is harness bug 3's race — whether the OS has already reset the Darwin
platform register in a given worker decides whether a word that READS x18 is
comparable — and a word can move between those two buckets and nowhere else.
OBSERVED ON BOTH TIERS:
So the gate's coverage floor is their SUM, which is exact, rather than a
tolerance on `compared`, which would have hidden the same amount of real
loss. The first full-tier gate run FAILED on this before the invariant was
corrected — recorded here because a coverage rule nobody ever saw fire is a
coverage rule nobody has tested.
STAGE 2 OF THE GATE. Each entry is a deliberately WRONG model (see
src/mutate.rs) run over the clang-assembled self-test corpus, and the
number of comparisons on which the differential caught it.
A ZERO IS A GATE FAILURE, not a curiosity: it means the differential can no
longer see that class of error, and every `0 mismatches` it reports
afterwards is about a question it stopped asking. A number BELOW the
recorded one is also a failure — detection power ratchets up only.
Every mutation is a bug that actually escaped into this codebase. They are
the fault log, not a list of plausible errors.
nonvacuity.corpus: selftest.s, assembled by clang, 99 words x 3 profiles

_comment: REGRESSION tier. Replays the committed population-fast.txt — no scan, so
it costs ~2 s of sweep and is byte-identical on every host. Covers the
same 86 opcodes as the full tier over a smaller population.
A frozen list cannot discover a form the decoder newly admits; that is
what the full tier is for.
DISCOVERY tier. Rescans the 2^32 encoding space and re-stratifies, so it
sees forms a decoder or semantics change has newly admitted. The scan
walks 320M indices to reach the rare opcodes and costs ~10 s; the sweep
costs another ~10 s. This is the tier whose numbers are quoted.
The exclusion counts the full tier produced, recorded so a LATER run that
quietly swallows a class into an exclusion is visible as movement here.
The authoritative explanation of each class — what it is, why it exists,
and which harness bug produced it — is the BLIND SPOTS header in
src/main.rs, which is normative: if a limitation is not listed there, the
harness is claiming to cover it.
These are informational: the gate fails on `coverage_floor`, which is the
same information stated as coverage rather than as loss.
